props.title: Phone

sections.content: Phone (2002) stands as a pivotal entry in the early 2000s Korean horror wave, following the massive success of Ring (1998) from Japan. Director Ahn Byeong-ki crafts a technophobic nightmare about a cursed cell phone number that kills its owners, building on themes established in One Missed Call (2003) and Pulse (2001). The film's strength lies in its atmospheric tension and commentary on Korea's rapid technological advancement, while incorporating traditional ghost story elements similar to A Tale of Two Sisters (2003).

sections.content: Korean horror cinema of the early 2000s excelled at blending modern anxieties with traditional supernatural elements. Phone follows journalist Ji-won Song who receives a mysterious phone number that leads to a series of deaths. Like Dark Water (2002) and The Eye (2002), the film uses a female protagonist to explore themes of isolation and technological alienation in rapidly modernizing Asian societies.

The film's technical achievements in sound design and visual effects influenced later technological horror films like Shutter (2004) and The Red Shoes (2005). Director Ahn Byeong-ki's use of ring tones and electronic interference as horror devices created a template for future tech-horror films like White: The Melody of Death (2011). sections.content: Phone masterfully bridges traditional Korean ghost stories with modern technological fears. The film's approach influenced later works like 4bia (2008) and Coming Soon (2008), which continued exploring the intersection of modern communication technology and supernatural horror. The film's success helped establish the template for technology-based Asian horror that would influence Western remakes like The Ring (2002) and Pulse (2006).
